law_name: Act on the Introduction of the Euro (Zakon o uvedbi eura, ZUE)
description: Adopted by the National Assembly on 26 October 2006, during Janša's first government, and published in the Official Gazette No. 114/2006 of 9 November 2006. It sets out the procedures for introducing the euro as Slovenia's currency, including the period of dual circulation of the tolar and the euro from 1 to 14 January 2007.
significance: Slovenia adopted the euro on 1 January 2007, the first of the countries that joined the EU in 2004 to do so (European Commission).

law_name: Fiscal Balance Act (Zakon za uravnoteženje javnih financ, ZUJF)
description: Omnibus austerity act of Janša's second government, adopted by the National Assembly on 11 May 2012 and in force from 31 May 2012 (Official Gazette No. 40/2012). It amended dozens of laws, including those on health insurance, public-sector pay and social transfers, to reduce public spending.
significance: The core of the 2012 fiscal consolidation during the euro-area debt crisis. Al Jazeera reported that the austerity policies had provoked mass strikes and protests, and Alenka Bratušek promised a break from them when the National Assembly replaced Janša in February 2013.

law_name: Act Amending the Waters Act (Zakon o spremembah in dopolnitvah Zakona o vodah, ZV-1G)
description: Amendment passed by the National Assembly at the end of March 2021, under Janša's third government, in a shortened procedure. Its most contested provision allowed 'public infrastructure' to be built near the banks of waterways and on the coast; environmental groups collected signatures for a referendum.
significance: Rejected in the legislative referendum of 11 July 2021 with almost 700,000 votes against and just over 100,000 in favour, on a turnout of about 46% (OBC Transeuropa), at the start of Slovenia's EU Council presidency.

law_name: Act on Interventions for the Development of Slovenia (Zakon o interventnih ukrepih za razvoj Slovenije, the 'development act')
description: Package tabled before the government took office by deputies of NSi, SLS, Fokus, the Democrats and Resni.ca and passed with SDS votes. It includes a cap on social-security contributions for higher salaries (the 'development cap', razvojna kapica) and, according to Janša, an option to cut taxes on energy products for nine months. Employers' organisations and doctors' organisations supported it; the trade unions opposed it (24ur).
significance: Its entry into force is suspended: the National Assembly declared the unions' referendum request inadmissible, the Constitutional Court annulled that decision, and voters will decide in a subsequent legislative referendum on 6 December 2026. Janša describes it as the basis of his government's economic programme.

law_name: Act Amending the Parliamentary Inquiries Act (Zakon o spremembah in dopolnitvah Zakona o parlamentarni preiskavi, ZPPre-B)
description: Tabled in mid-May 2026 by SDS and NSi–SLS–Fokus deputies, before Janša was elected Prime Minister, and adopted by the National Assembly on 26 May 2026. Among other things it limits the possibility of challenging an act ordering a parliamentary inquiry before the Constitutional Court; its sponsors said the safeguards added by the previous government caused serious delays in setting up inquiry committees.
significance: Voters rejected it in a legislative referendum on 11 October 2026 (51.26% against, 48.74% for, according to the State Election Commission's figures reported by RTV SLO), so it did not enter into force.

law_name: Amendment to the Local Elections Act (Zakon o lokalnih volitvah): voting rights of third-country nationals
description: Coalition amendment that removes the right of third-country nationals to vote in municipal elections, leaving it to Slovenian and other EU citizens. Opponents filed a referendum initiative but withdrew it before collecting signatures, so the law took effect (24ur).
significance: It applies to the local elections of November 2026; the opposition has asked the Constitutional Court to review it. In a consultative referendum on 11 October 2026, 55.30% of voters supported limiting local voting rights to Slovenian and EU citizens.

law_name: Act on Temporary Measures for a More Effective Long-Term Care System (Zakon o začasnih ukrepih za učinkovitejše izvajanje sistema dolgotrajne oskrbe)
description: Government bill adopted by the National Assembly on 18 September 2026 by 61 votes to none and in force since 1 October 2026. Residents of care homes without a long-term care decision now pay the same as those already in the system, people disadvantaged since 1 December 2025 can receive a credit, and full-time employees providing long-term care and home help receive a supplement of €300 gross a month.
significance: A cross-party measure: 24ur reported that the opposition supported its basic solutions in principle.

law_name: Act on Specialised Bodies for Corruption Offences and Organised Crime (Zakon o specializiranih organih za obravnavo korupcijskih kaznivih dejanj in organiziranega kriminala, SKOK)
description: Passed by the National Assembly under the urgent procedure on 24 September 2026 by 47 votes to 35. It turns the Specialised State Prosecutor's Office into a prosecution body for corruption and organised crime, creates a Specialised Court with district-court status in Ljubljana (appeals to the Higher Court in Maribor), redefines the catalogue of offences and abolishes the judicial investigation in these cases. It entered into force in October 2026 and applies from 1 July 2027.
significance: A flagship commitment of the coalition, promoted by the Democrats, who hold the justice ministry. The coalition calls it a key step against corruption; the opposition warned of the subordination of prosecution to politics, and the judiciary and prosecution criticised it as insufficiently thought through (RTV SLO).

description: Adopted by the government on 10 September and by the National Assembly on 1 October 2026: revenue of €16.5 billion (+6.3%), expenditure of €18.8 billion (+6.2%) and a deficit of €2.2 billion, or 2.9% of GDP. It adds €296 million for defence, which the government says brings defence spending to 2.03% of GDP, and €320 million for projects under the EU recovery plan.
significance: The first budget act of the fourth Janša government. The finance minister says the deficit complies with the fiscal rules; the Fiscal Council said the revision is a further departure from Slovenia's medium-term fiscal commitments and contains no measures for a lasting improvement.
